title: Dimension-inductive gluing of local regular alteration covers
statement: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an integral quasi-excellent Noetherian local scheme with closed point $s$, and let $\ell$ be invertible on $S$ [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $Z\subseteq S$ be nowhere dense. Suppose $(P_i\to S)_{i\in I}$ is a finite covering family in $\operatorname{alt}/S$ for the topology of $\ell'$-alterations [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology], and for every $i$ an open $V_i\subseteq P_i$ contains the whole fibre over $s$, is regular, and carries a specified strict normal crossings boundary supported on the inverse image of $Z$ [def-weil-open-immersion], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Assume also that for every non-closed point $t\in S$ there is a separated etale morphism of finite presentation $e_t:T_t\to S$ and a point $t'\in T_t$ over $t$ inducing an isomorphism of residue fields, together with a finite covering family $(Q_{tj}\to T_t)_j$ in $\operatorname{alt}/T_t$ whose sources are regular and whose specified strict normal crossings boundaries are supported on the inverse image of $e_t^{-1}Z$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Then there is a finite set $F$ of non-closed points such that $(T_t\times_S(S\setminus\{s\})\to S\setminus\{s\})_{t\in F}$ is completely decomposed over the punctured scheme $S\setminus\{s\}$ (the closed point need not lie under any $T_t$), and after taking reduced dominant components of the $V_i$ and of the composites $Q_{tj}\to T_t\to S$ for $t\in F$, these sources form a finite covering family in $\operatorname{alt}/S$; every source is regular and its boundary is a strict normal crossings boundary supported on the inverse image of $Z$.

source.place: Correction of the closed-fibre step of Expose III Proposition 6.2, printed p.44 (where ILO invokes II 4.1.1, proved only for alt): on each $P_i$ the family consisting of $V_i$ and the base changes $P_i\times_ST_t$ ($t\in F$) is completely decomposed etale, hence covering by Expose II Definitions 2.1.1--2.1.2 and 2.3.1; finiteness of $F$ by II Corollary 2.2.4 on $S\setminus\{s\}$; then compose with the $Q_{tj}$ and refine. The pointed-etale spreading pattern is that of the first paragraph of the proof of III 6.2, pp.43--44.

proof.text: Put $U=S\setminus\{s\}$. Every $P_i$ is finite type over $S$ by the definition of $\operatorname{alt}/S$, hence Noetherian. The opens $U$ and $V_i$ are Noetherian, in particular quasi-compact; since their targets are Noetherian their open immersions are quasi-compact, and $V_i\to P_i$ is finite type. A finite-presentation morphism is finite type: its affine presentations have finitely many algebra generators, and it is quasi-compact by definition. Consequently every $T_t$ is Noetherian and finite type over $S$, and every $Q_{tj}$ is Noetherian and finite type over $S$ by composition. These observations justify all subsequent applications of the Noetherian cover and dominant-part results.

source.place: III Proposition 6.2, pp.43--44, finiteness bookkeeping for the pointed-etale neighborhoods; Stacks Tags 01T6, 01OW, 01OZ, 01T0, 01T2 and 01TP

proof.text: The base changes $T_t\times_SU\to U$ are etale. For $u\in U$, choose the neighborhood indexed by $t=u$. Its specified point $t^{\prime}$ gives a point over $u$ in $T_u\times_SU$ with residue field exactly $\kappa(u)$, since restriction to an open changes no local ring. Thus this family is completely decomposed. Apply the completely-decomposed finite-subcover lemma to the Noetherian scheme $U$ to obtain a finite subset $F\subseteq |U|$ for which it remains completely decomposed. If $U$ is empty take $F=\varnothing$.

source.place: II Corollary 2.2.4, p.27, applied to the punctured scheme; III Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44

proof.text: All schemes that will occur as covering sources can be regarded over $S$. Indeed $S_{\mathrm{md}}=S$, and the etale comparison in the dominant-part lemma gives $(T_t)_{\mathrm{md}}\simeq T_t\times_SS=T_t$. Hence $T_t$ is reduced and all its components dominate $S$. The etale residue-field lemma, applied on affine charts, gives finite residue extensions, so $T_t\in\operatorname{alt}/S$. Likewise $(P_i)_{\mathrm{md}}=P_i$ and applying that comparison to the open etale immersion $V_i\to P_i$ gives $(V_i)_{\mathrm{md}}=V_i$; its generic residue extensions over $S$ are inherited from $P_i$. Finally a generic point of $Q_{tj}$ maps to a generic point of $T_t$, hence to that of $S$, and its residue degree over $S$ is finite by the tower formula. Thus $V_i$ and the composites $Q_{tj}\to S$ are objects of $\operatorname{alt}/S$.

source.place: II 1.1.10 and 1.2.2--1.2.6, pp.24--25; Stacks Tag 00U3 for finite etale residue extensions

proof.text: For each $t\in F$, Step 3 has placed $T_t$ in $\operatorname{alt}/S$; it is Noetherian by Step 1. Apply alteration-site localization to $T_t\to S$. It identifies $\operatorname{alt}/T_t$ with the slice of $\operatorname{alt}/S$ at $T_t$ and identifies their topologies. Consequently the given covering family $(Q_{tj}\to T_t)_j$ is also a covering family with ambient category $\operatorname{alt}/S$. This changes neither the schemes $Q_{tj}$ nor their specified boundaries.

source.place: II Proposition 1.1.10, proof of Proposition 1.2.6, and 2.3.1, pp.24--28; the pointed-etale covering step in III Proposition 6.2, pp.43--44

proof.text: Fix $i$. Write $W_{it}=P_i\times_ST_t$ for $t\in F$. By the etale comparison of dominant parts and $(P_i)_{\mathrm{md}}=P_i$, its dominant part equals this ordinary fibre product. Its projection to $P_i$ is etale, and it is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$ by the categorical fibre-product statement. Consider $\{V_i\to P_i\}\cup\{W_{it}\to P_i:t\in F\}$. A point $p$ over $s$ lies in $V_i$ by hypothesis and lifts with identical residue field. If the image of $p$ is $u\ne s$, Step 2 supplies $t\in F$ and $z\in T_t$ over $u$ with $\kappa(z)=\kappa(u)$. Compose $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(p)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\cong\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\to T_t$ (the point $z$ of Step 2, which need not be the specified point $t^{\prime}$ over $t$). Together with the point $p$ of $P_i$, the fibre-product universal property gives a section over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(p)$ of the fibre of $W_{it}\to P_i$. Its image has residue field $\kappa(p)$: the section makes that residue field embed back into $\kappa(p)$ over $\kappa(p)$, forcing equality. The family is therefore completely decomposed etale, hence $\ell^{\prime}$-decomposed (degree $1$) and covering by the definition of the topology.

source.place: Correction of III Proposition 6.2, p.44: replace its II 4.1.1 invocation by II 2.1.1--2.1.2 and 2.3.1, pp.26--28, on each $P_i$

proof.text: For each $i,t$, pull the covering $(Q_{tj}\to T_t)_j$ of Step 4 back along $W_{it}\to T_t$ inside $\operatorname{alt}/S$. The cover calculus identifies its sources $R_{itj}$ with the reduced dominant parts of the usual fibre products $W_{it}\times_{T_t}Q_{tj}$, and says they cover $W_{it}$. Compose with the covering of $P_i$ in Step 5, keeping $V_i$ on its branch, and then compose with $(P_i\to S)_i$. The resulting finite family $\{V_i\to S\}_i\cup\{R_{itj}\to S\}_{i,t,j}$ is covering. Each $R_{itj}$ has its projection to $Q_{tj}$. Hence this covering family refines $\{V_i\to S\}_i\cup\{Q_{tj}\to S\}_{t,j}$, whose generated sieve contains the covering sieve just constructed. A supersieve of a covering sieve is covering: its pullback along each arrow of the smaller sieve contains the identity and is therefore maximal, so the transitivity axiom applies. No regularity of $R_{itj}$ is claimed or needed.

source.place: II 1.2.6 and 2.3.1, pp.25,28; composition and refinement replace the unsupported prime-to-ell closed-fibre shrinking step in III 6.2, p.44

proof.text: The covering sources $V_i$ and $Q_{tj}$ are regular by the hypotheses, and are Noetherian by Step 1. The regular-normal-components theorem makes each a finite disjoint union of open-and-closed integral components. Its reduced component scheme is precisely that open subscheme; because the whole source is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$ by Step 3, every nonempty component is dominant over $S$ and has finite generic residue degree. The component-cover clause of the alteration calculus and composition therefore replace the finite covering of Step 6 by the finite family of these reduced dominant components. Empty sources contribute no components. Regularity on each component follows from the unchanged local rings of an open subscheme.

source.place: III 6.2, p.44, disjoint integral regular components near the special fibre; Stacks Tags 0569 and 033M for regularity, normality and components

proof.text: Restrict each specified boundary to each selected open-and-closed component $C$ of its source $X$. Every integral boundary component of $X$ is contained in exactly one such $C$, since its irreducible support cannot meet two disjoint opens. Discard the boundary components lying outside $C$. On $C$ the ideal of the boundary is the same effective Cartier radical ideal as on $X$, all nonempty intersections have the same local rings, and the ambient and intersection dimensions at their points are unchanged. Thus all clauses of the strict-normal-crossings definition hold after restriction, including the empty-boundary case. The support is the intersection of the old support with $C$, and so remains contained in the inverse image of $Z$, since the composite $Q_{tj}\to S$ pulls $Z$ back to the inverse image of $e_t^{-1}Z$. These are precisely the sources and boundaries asserted in the conclusion, together with the finite $F$ already obtained in Step 2.

source.place: III 6.1--6.2, pp.43--44; VIII 4.1.2--4.1.4(i) and Remark 4.2.2(i), pp.117--119, restriction of the defining boundary conditions

proof_origin.place: III Proposition 6.2, printed pp.43--44, corrected using II 1.2.5--1.2.6, 2.1.1--2.1.2, Corollary 2.2.4 and 2.3.1; the prime-to-ell case is proved by explicit gluing, not II 4.1.1.

from.place: Expose III Proposition 6.2, p.44: the local descent is completed by induction on the dimension of the local base, spreading the covers obtained at non-closed points to pointed etale neighborhoods and combining them with the regular neighborhood of the closed fibre.

split_report.summary: Proved finite punctured completely-decomposed extraction, checked all sources and the ambient alteration categories, constructed a completely-decomposed covering on each P_i, and composed/refined covers before taking regular clopen components and restricting SNC boundaries. Reused existing DAG lemmas and isolated one genuine comparison lemma, alteration-site localization, as a statement-only node. The generic Mathlib localization theorem is only a candidate because the scheme-category equivalence must also be proved. Preserved the corrected statement and source warning about II 4.1.1. All cited statements read and quoted in citations.json.

Steps 1-3 check: everything is Noetherian and finite type, F comes from the completely-decomposed finite subcover on U (F empty when S is a field), and the étale clause of the dominant-part lemma gives (T_t)_md = T_t, (V_i)_md = V_i and (W_it)_md = W_it. Step 4 is the only use of the new node. Step 5's family {V_i, P_i×_S T_t} on each P_i is completely decomposed, so it is a type (i) generator. Step 6 composes the covers and proves the refinement through sieve axiom (iii). Step 7 takes the clopen integral components. Step 8 restricts the SNC boundary, checked against every clause of def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary.
